observation_summary: The method DiscreteDistribution.sample(int) throws an ArrayStoreException because it attempts to create an array using the class of the first element in the list, which fails when subsequent elements are of different (sub)types.
hypothesis: The ArrayStoreException occurs because DiscreteDistribution.sample(int) uses the class of the first element in the 'singletons' list to create the result array via reflection. The fix should be to use the generic type T (or Object.class) for the array creation instead of the class of the first element.

This is an algorithmic flaw in how the result container is initialized.
